title: Membership Policy

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Fora Advisors build travel businesses by delivering exceptional service to their clients. Fora has built a structure to support and reward advisor growth and continued investment in their book of business. The structure, benefits, and expectations related to advisor status are outlined below to help advisors make the most of their experience at Fora.

Below is an overview of advisor status, how to qualify and maintain status, commission structure, and the guidelines around building a team. It also includes information on membership cancellations and refunds. Together this provides a clear and supportive framework to help advisors thrive at Fora.

sections.heading: Eligibility
paragraphs: Fora Advisors must be at least 18 years of age and have the legal capacity to enter into a binding contract.
If at any time Fora becomes aware that an advisor does not meet these requirements, Fora may suspend or terminate that advisor’s participation in the program at its sole discretion.

sections.heading: Advisor Status
paragraphs: Fora Advisor status provides access to different benefits, programs, and experiences based on sales, community engagement, and demonstrated expertise. Advisor status can be achieved at any point during the year and is valid through the end of the following year, except for Certified status which is retained for life. The status qualification period resets every calendar year on January 1st.
As advisor status changes, access to relevant benefits, programs and experiences will update to reflect current status.
Learn how to achieve each status and the associated benefits here.

sections.heading: Annual Booking Volume
paragraphs: Advanced, Pro, and Fora X advisor statuses have Annual Booking Volume requirements (total commissionable booking value in a year, typically before taxes, fees, and non-commissionable items). Advisors can find their Annual Booked Volume on the Dashboard in Portal.

All Eligible Travel counts toward Annual Booking Value unless the associated commission rate is less than 5% (or less than 2.5% for private flight charters). If the commission rate is less than 5% (or less than 2.5% for private flight charters), the dollar amount of commission will count toward Annual Booking Volume, rather than the total commissionable value.
Commissionable flights booked with Fora Flights are an exception. The base fare of commissionable flights booked with Fora Flights will count toward your commission volume.
Please note this only applies to bookings made with Fora Flights. Flights booked with outside flights vendors still need to meet the 5% threshold.
What does this  mean?
A $5000 booking with a 5% (or more) commission rate or a $5,000 private flight charter with a 2.5% commission rate will contribute the full $5,000 booking value toward Annual Booking Volume.
A $5000 booking with a 2% commission rate will contribute $100—or 2% of the $5000 booking value—toward Annual Booking Volume.
Note: Annual Booking Volume adjusts as modifications and cancellations are made to existing bookings. These changes could impact advisor status.
Learn more about Annual Booking Volume and Eligible Travel in the Terms of Membership & Service in Portal settings.

sections.heading: Enhanced Commission Split
paragraphs: Advisors who book more than $300,000 in Annual Booking Volume during the calendar year will receive an enhanced 80/20 commission split. An enhanced commission split can be achieved at any point during the year and will apply to Eligible Travel from the first booking that brings an advisor’s Annual Booking Volume over $300,000 for the remainder of the year and to all bookings made the following year. If an advisor doesn’t book $300,000 in that second year, their commission split will reset to 70/30 on January 1st of the third year.

If an advisor receives an enhanced commission split for the first time but then has cancellations or modifications that bring their Annual Booking Volume below $300,000, the standard 70/30 commission split will retroactively apply to all previous bookings where the 80/20 commission split was used. The enhanced 80/20 commission split will only resume once the advisor reaches $300,000 in bookings again within the same calendar year. On occasion, an advisor may have been overpaid because of the adjustment from an Enhanced Commission Split to a standard split. In these cases, Fora will offset overpayments against future commissions or request repayment.

To maintain the enhanced commission split, advisors are recommended to aim for more than $300,000 in Annual Booking Volume to limit the impact of cancellations and modifications which are often beyond an advisor’s control.

sections.heading: Account Sharing
paragraphs: Fora does not allow account sharing. Only one advisor per account is permitted. If a Fora Advisor has a business partner, each person must have their own account.

sections.heading: Additional Business Support
paragraphs: As an advisor’s business grows, advisors may request to bring on additional support. Before considering support, Fora highly recommends ensuring that workflows and processes are well established in order to maximize efficiency. Fora Advisors may request support options after reaching Pro, however it is highly encouraged to wait until advisors reach Fora X.
Delegation is the capability to allow an identified individual to access the ‘Primary Advisor’s’ account. Access limitations include:
Financial data, commissions, or performance dashboards
Leads, training, community spaces, or events
Account settings or web profile management
Email functionality or support contact tools
Learn more about delegation here.

sections.heading: Uncertified, Certified and Advanced Advisors
paragraphs: Uncertified, Certified, and Advanced advisors are not eligible for a ‘business partner’ with Portal access.

sections.heading: Pro and X Advisors
paragraphs: Pro and X advisors may have a ‘Team Member’ with Portal access to support their business.
Additional Requirements:
Advisors choosing to work with a ‘Team Member’ must submit an application.
The advisor Team Lead must have an established LLC with additional E&O insurance.
Both Team Lead and Team Member must have 2 FA turned on on all devices
Team Lead must pass the Identify and Business verification process
Team Member must have a Fora email account and an active Membership
Team Member must complete and pass Identity Verification within 72 hrs following access to the Fora email account

As defined in the Account Sharing policy, Fora does not allow password sharing or account sharing in any form. Each allocated ‘Team Member’ must utilize their Fora email for any outside communications. They must also clearly identify themselves as the advisors ‘Team Member’ or other respective language when working on a ‘Primary Advisor’’s Booking.

sections.heading: Team Lead Liability
paragraphs: The ‘Primary Advisor’ assumes full responsibility for any and all actions taken by the identified Team Member. Both parties are expected to adhere to all Fora Community Policies and Guidelines unless specifically noted otherwise. Fora is unable to support the process of creating team agreements, handling team disputes, or team formation agreements. Please consult professionals on any questions you have regarding taxes, legal agreements, or hiring standards in your state/country.

sections.heading: Account & Client Ownership
paragraphs: The lead advisor and each Team Member are solely responsible for agreeing in writing on their working relationship and internal compensation structure, including how revenue is shared between them. Fora does not mediate or enforce these internal arrangements.

By default, any client profile, client data and/or booking that is created, reported, or managed in a Team Member’s Fora account is part of that Team Member’s book of business and will remain with that account if the arrangement between the Lead Advisor and Team Member ends.

Advisors may not use Fora-managed community channels to advertise that they are seeking Team Members or to promote Team Member support opportunities. Advisors may not actively solicit or pressure advisors who are currently part of another Lead Advisor’s team to leave that team to join their own.
For additional details on adding a Team Member to your account, please visit the help center here.

sections.heading: Advisor Reviews
paragraphs: Reviews help build trust and transparency across the Fora community and may be required to achieve advisor status. Fora values client feedback and will not remove a review solely because it reflects negatively on an advisor.
Reviews can only be submitted post travel and must be submitted by December 31st to count towards your certification for the calendar year.
Learn more about reviews here.

sections.heading: Voluntary Cancellation
paragraphs: Fora Advisors can cancel their membership at any time in Portal. Account access will remain active until the end of the current billing cycle. After the final billing cycle, the  account—including Portal access and the @fora.travel email—will be deactivated.
Please note that refunds are not provided in the case of early cancellation, including prorated refunds.
To avoid automatic renewal and future charges, advisors must cancel or modify their Advisor Plan in Portal before the current billing period:

sections.heading: Go to Advisor Portal Settings
paragraphs: Scroll down to Your Subscription and click on the Go to Billing Portal button
View the subscription and the renewal date at the top of the page
Fora will remind you of any upcoming membership payment five days before the charge in an email sent to both personal and fora.travel email addresses.

sections.heading: Involuntary Cancellation
paragraphs: Fora reserves the right to terminate an advisor’s membership with up to three days' notice and the advisor will no longer have access to their Fora email address and Portal upon termination. This is especially applicable if the advisor is moving to another agency and plans to begin booking under a different IATA.
If Fora believes an advisor is in violation of the Terms of Membership & Service, Community Guidelines, or any Fora policies, membership fees will not be refunded.
Learn more about what happens to bookings and commissions once a membership is cancelled here.

sections.heading: Referral Policy
paragraphs: Fora Advisors may refer prospective advisors to join the Fora community. Referrals are intended to support thoughtful community growth and should reflect genuine belief in the value of becoming a Fora Advisor.
This referral policy will go live on May 6th, 2026. Only referral sign ups made after this time are qualified for the program.
Advisors may make up to ten (10) qualified referrals per calendar year.

A “qualified referral” is defined as a newly identified individual who completes the advisor application process using the referring advisor’s code and signs up as an active Fora advisor. A qualified referral cannot have had a Fora membership in the past.

Advisors who have made five (5) or more referrals in a calendar year without any resulting client bookings from those referred advisors may be restricted from making additional referrals for the remainder of that year.

Fora reserves the right to review referral activity and take appropriate action, including withholding incentives, limiting referral privileges, or reclassifying participation in the program, where activity is deemed inconsistent with this policy or the broader Policies and Community Guidelines.
Note: Referral rewards are reported as cash-equivalent gifts for 1099-NEC purposes.
For more information please refer to the Referrals Help Center Article.

sections.heading: Refunds
paragraphs: Advisors can cancel their membership within 14 days of signup for a full refund. After 14 days, membership fees cannot be refunded.

title: Booking & Commissions Policy

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Fora Advisors earn income through commissions paid by travel partners for selling travel.

Fora centrally manages partner invoicing, commission collection, and reconciliation for accurate and timely payouts on the advisor’s behalf. Part of our mission is to make the financial administrative processes of being a travel advisor as seamless as possible and focus on serving your clients and selling more travel.

To ensure that advisors are paid as quickly as possible, we have outlined key processes and guidelines around using Fora’s IATA, reporting commissions, managing net rate and takeover bookings, and handling additional earnings. This policy also covers expectations around self-booking, personal credit card use, and advisor responsibility in the event of chargebacks or fraud.
These practices are in place to help protect advisors’ businesses and maintain trust with both clients and partners.

sections.heading: Fora’s IATA
paragraphs: Advisors must complete and pass the Identity Verification process before being eligible to book travel using Fora’s IATA number.

Fora Advisors should only share Fora’s IATA number when needed to complete a booking or with partners. It should not be shared otherwise including but not limited to email signatures, personal websites and business cards.

sections.heading: Reporting Commissions
paragraphs: In order to ensure timely invoicing and payout, advisors must submit bookings made outside of Portal to submit@fora.travel or upload the booking confirmation to Portal within 2 business days (48 hours) of partner confirmation.

sections.heading: Late Booking Submissions
paragraphs: Bookings submitted 30-90 days after client checkout may result in further payment delays or, in some cases, it may not be collectible. If Fora is able to collect the commission from travel partners, it will be paid out to the advisor.
Commission for bookings submitted more than 90 days after checkout may not be paid.

sections.heading: Submissions Under Review
paragraphs: If a booking submission is incomplete and the advisor does not respond to the Commissions team within 30 days of being contacted for more details, the booking will not be logged. This booking will not count towards the advisor’s Annual Booking Volume, and the advisor will need to resubmit the booking if they still wish to have it logged.

sections.heading: Payment of Commissions
paragraphs: All payments from travel partners, including commission payments, bonuses and individual incentive programs, etc. must be paid directly to Fora by the partner. Fora Advisors should never receive payment directly from the travel partner. If working with a new partner, the advisor should introduce the partner to Fora by emailing support@fora.travel.
Learn more about onboarding a new travel partner here.

sections.heading: Additional Earnings Subject to Split
paragraphs: In addition to commission earned on bookings, partners may support Additional Earnings opportunities (i.e. promotions, incentives, bonus commissions, or the ability to add a service charge). These types of earnings and the associated payments are subject to the advisor’s commission split with Fora.
Advisors should submit these Additional Earnings along with the associated booking(s) to ensure they are paid out correctly.
Additional earnings could include:
Bonus commissions for meeting sales thresholds or goals
Added service charges (e.g. the Agency Service Change on a booking on Expedia TAAP or VAX)
Any additional markups or commission added to a booking made directly with a partner or wholesaler

sections.heading: Desk Operations Commission Split
paragraphs: Bookings made through Fora's desk operations (e.g. Fora Cruise Desk) may be subject to a different commission split than the standard advisor split. The split will be communicated to advisors and determined by the Desk prior to service.

sections.heading: Non-Commissionable Bookings
paragraphs: Advisors are allowed to facilitate non-commissionable bookings for clients. Since these bookings are not eligible for commission, they should not be submitted for logging. Keep in mind that non-commissionable bookings do not count towards an advisor’s Annual Booking Volume.
Learn more about non-commissionable bookings here.

sections.heading: Commission Rebates & Discounting
paragraphs: Unless expressly permitted by the terms and conditions of a travel supplier, Fora Advisors may not advertise, promise, or give any “rebate” or discount on the travel service to a client by using, reducing, or giving back any portion of the commission or other earnings payable to the advisor or to Fora on a booking.

This includes but is not limited to cash or cash-equivalent incentives (such as personal payments, gift cards, credits, or price-matching by the advisor) that reduce the client’s price, unless it’s part of a Fora-approved promotion in writing.

Advisors may not ask for, accept, or promote net or reduced-commission rates (including “friends and family” or similar promotions) in order to lower a client’s price by waiving or reducing commission. This includes converting a commissionable (gross) rate to a net rate or agreeing to a lower commission so the client pays less. All use of net rates must follow Fora’s Net Rate Policy and may not be used as a workaround for client discounts.

sections.heading: Net Rates
paragraphs: Some travel partners offer both gross rate (price with commission included) and net rate (price with commission excluded) payment options. Net rates are most frequently found with DMCs and independent hotels outside of the U.S.

When working with a net rate booking, the advisor is responsible for adding the commission on top of the net rate provided by the partner. Fora headquarters invoices the client for the total of the net rate and the commission, collects the full amount from the client, pays the net rate to the travel partner, and applies the commission split for the advisor.

In order to submit a net rate request, please complete a net rate submission form and use the net rate calculator to determine the gross rate to charge your client. Prior to submitting your request, ensure that it meets the following requirements:
Advisors must be certified to charge a net rate.
The net rate booking must exceed $1500 before commission is added.
If the booking is below this threshold, advisors are encouraged to consider finding an alternative partner, or foregoing commission and charging a planning fee instead.
Advisors can only submit one booking per net rate form. Fora will issue no more than  two invoices to the client per submission.

For example, if the advisor has made four net rate bookings with four different travel partners, they should submit each booking using a separate net rate form. For each submission, Fora will generate up to two invoices to the client.
Advisors must charge a minimum commission of 10% for all net rates and 12% for all preferred partner DMCs found in Portal.
A 12% commission baseline is recommended for all net rate bookings to cover the increased potential taxes and fees involved in these transactions.
The payment method from the client to Fora and from Fora to the travel partner must match to avoid any risk of chargeback.

Advisors should confirm with the partner what payment method they require, and select that method when filling out the net rate form. For example, if the travel partner only accepts bank transfers, Fora can only accept bank transfers from the client.
Learn more about net rates here.
Learn more about planning fees here!

sections.heading: Booking Integrity
paragraphs: Fora Advisors are prohibited from taking over, or canceling and rebooking travel services arranged through another travel advisor (whether or not an affiliate of Fora), including their own travel.

Advisors are also strictly prohibited from submitting themselves or members of their household through Fora’s Client Lead Programs (CLP) or any related lead distribution channels. All CLP submissions must represent genuine prospective clients external to the advisor.

sections.heading: Takeover Booking
paragraphs: A takeover booking is when an advisor retroactively adds Fora’s IATA number to an existing booking that was made directly with the partner or property. This means the advisor becomes the Agent of Record for that booking, allowing them to collect the commission and provide the client any available preferred partner  perks.
To determine the eligibility of a takeover booking, please confirm the following:
The booking was made directly with the hotel
The booking wasn’t paid for with points or miles
Note: Even if the booking is deemed eligible based on the above, Marriott hotel bookings are excluded from this process and have a strict no takeover policy.
Learn more about how to take over a booking here.
Learn more about how to take over a cruise booking here.

sections.heading: Self Booking
paragraphs: Fora Advisors are entrepreneurs who build travel advisory businesses with a diverse client base. Clients may include friends, extended family, or people from your broader network.

While self-booking (bookings made for the purpose of personal travel) are permitted, Fora Advisors must not exclusively book travel for themselves indefinitely. Advisors must log commissionable bookings for a minimum of two (2) additional unique clients (not including the advisor) within the first six (6) months on the Fora platform (new members) or the first six (6) months of each calendar year (existing members).
A unique client is defined as an individual who is not the advisor themselves. Each unique client must have their own distinct traveler profile and payment method within Portal.
A booking is considered 'logged' by making a booking directly through the 'Book' tab within Fora's advisor portal and/or submitting a qualified, commissionable booking through the 'Manage' tab.
Important Note: As outlined in the 'Booking Integrity' policy, you may not take over, or cancel and rebook travel services arranged through another travel advisor for the benefits of a self booking.
Learn more about how to submit a booking here.
Learn more about commissionable bookings here.

sections.heading: Advisor’s Credit Card Use
paragraphs: Fora Advisors are not allowed to use credit or debit cards in their own control (whether personal or business cards) for any client travel related bookings or expenses.

sections.heading: Fraud and Chargebacks
paragraphs: Fora Advisors care deeply about clients and their travel experiences, as well as maintaining trusted relationships with our partners. Unfortunately, the travel industry is a target for fraud, including chargebacks. When client issues such as fraud or chargebacks arise, the advisor’s engagement, professionalism, and responsiveness to communications and requests make all the difference in resolving these matters quickly.

Fora recognizes how concerning it can be when fraud or chargebacks happen. If Fora becomes aware of a high risk booking Fora will reach out to the advisor for details about the clients and bookings requesting additional documentation.
Advisors who have been the victim of fraud or something that seems suspicious (whether it’s the behavior of a client, partner or another advisor) should email support@fora.travel.

sections.heading: Fora Advisor Responsibility in Client Disputes
paragraphs: If unable to resolve client fraud or chargeback issues with the client and the partner, the advisor will be held responsible for any resulting losses incurred by the partner and passed on to Fora. If Fora reaches out to an advisor for additional information related to fraud or chargebacks, a response is required within 72 hours. Failure to respond in a timely manner could result in an advisor’s bookings being cancelled, particularly if there are fraud concerns.

sections.heading: Financial Accountability
paragraphs: If a chargeback dispute is not resolved in favor of the partner:
The advisor is responsible for reimbursing the partner the full amount of the chargeback.
Fora reserves the right to pay the partner directly on the advisor’s behalf and recover the amount by offsetting future commissions due to the advisor.
Fora Advisors are responsible for the bookings that they make and the clients that they manage.
Learn more about detecting and preventing fraud here.

advisor’s commission split with fora. advisors should submit these additional earnings along with the associated booking(s) to ensure they are paid out correctly. additional earnings could include: bonus commissions for meeting sales thresholds or goals added service charges (e.g. the agency service change on a booking on expedia taap or vax) any additional markups or commission added to a booking made directly with a partner or wholesaler desk operations commission split bookings made through fora's desk operations (e.g. fora cruise desk) may be subject to a different commission split than the standard advisor split. the split will be communicated to advisors and determined by the desk prior to service. non-commissionable bookings advisors are allowed to facilitate non-commissionable bookings for clients. since these bookings are not eligible for commission, they should not be submitted for logging. keep in mind that non-commissionable bookings do not count towards an advisor’s annual booking volume. learn more about non-commissionable bookings here. commission rebates & discounting unless expressly permitted by the terms and conditions of a travel supplier, fora advisors may not advertise, promise, or give any “rebate” or discount on the travel service to a client by using, reducing, or giving back any portion of the commission or other earnings payable to the advisor or to fora on a booking. this includes but is not limited to cash or cash-equivalent incentives (such as personal payments, gift cards, credits, or price-matching by the advisor) that reduce the client’s price, unless it’s part of a fora-approved promotion in writing. advisors may not ask for, accept, or promote net or reduced-commission rates (including “friends and family” or similar promotions) in order to lower a client’s price by waiving or reducing commission. this includes converting a commissionable (gross) rate to a net rate or agreeing to a lower commission so the client pays less. all use of net rates must follow fora’s net rate policy and may not be used as a workaround for client discounts. net rates some travel partners offer both gross rate (price with commission included) and net rate (price with commission excluded) payment options. net rates are most frequently found with dmcs and independent hotels outside of the u.s. when working with a net rate booking, the advisor is responsible for adding the commission on top of the net rate provided by the partner. fora headquarters invoices the client for the total of the net rate and the commission, collects the full amount from the client, pays the net rate to the travel partner, and applies the commission split for the advisor. in order to submit a net rate request, please complete a net rate submission form and use the net rate calculator to determine the gross rate to charge your client. prior to submitting your request, ensure that it meets the following requirements: advisors must be certified to charge a net rate. the net rate booking must exceed $1500 before commission is added. if the booking is below this threshold, advisors are encouraged to consider finding an alternative partner, or foregoing commission and charging a planning fee instead. advisors can only submit one booking per net rate form. fora will issue no more than  two invoices to the client per submission. for example, if the advisor has made four net rate bookings with four different travel partners, they should submit each booking using a separate net rate form. for each submission, fora will generate up to two invoices to the client. advisors must charge a minimum commission of 10% for all net rates and 12% for all preferred partner dmcs found in portal. a 12% commission baseline is recommended for all net rate bookings to cover the increased potential taxes and fees involved in these transactions. the payment method from the client to fora and from fora to the travel partner must match to avoid any risk of chargeback. advisors should confirm with the partner what payment method they require, and select that method when filling out the net rate form. for example, if the travel partner only accepts bank transfers, fora can only accept bank transfers from the client. learn more about net rates here. learn more about planning fees here! booking integrity fora advisors are prohibited from taking over, or canceling and rebooking travel services arranged through another travel advisor (whether or not an affiliate of fora), including their own travel. advisors are also strictly prohibited from submitting themselves or members of their household through fora’s client lead programs (clp) or any related lead distribution channels. all clp submissions must represent genuine prospective clients external to the advisor. takeover booking a takeover booking is when an advisor retroactively adds fora’s iata number to an existing booking that was made directly with the partner or property. this means the advisor becomes the agent of record for that booking, allowing them to collect the commission and provide the client any available preferred partner  perks. to determine the eligibility of a takeover booking, please confirm the following: the booking was made directly with the hotel the booking wasn’t paid for with points or miles note: even if the booking is deemed eligible based on the above, marriott hotel bookings are excluded from this process and have a strict no takeover policy. learn more about how to take over a booking here. learn more about how to take over a cruise booking here. self booking fora advisors are entrepreneurs who build travel advisory businesses with a diverse client base. clients may include (new members) or the first six (6) months of each calendar year (existing members). a unique client is defined as an individual who is not the advisor themselves. each unique client must have their own distinct traveler profile and payment method within portal. a booking is considered 'logged' by making a booking directly through the 'book' tab within fora's advisor portal and/or submitting a qualified, commissionable booking through the 'manage' tab. important note: as outlined in the 'booking integrity' policy, you may not take over, or cancel and rebook travel services arranged through another travel advisor for the benefits of a self booking. learn more about how to submit a booking here. learn more about commissionable bookings here. advisor’s credit card use fora advisors are not allowed to use credit or debit cards in their own control (whether personal or business cards) for any client travel related bookings or expenses. fraud and chargebacks fora advisors care deeply about clients and their travel experiences, as well as maintaining trusted relationships with our partners. unfortunately, the travel industry is a target for fraud, including chargebacks. when client issues such as fraud or chargebacks arise, the advisor’s engagement, professionalism, and responsiveness to communications and requests make all the difference in resolving these matters quickly. fora recognizes how concerning it can be when fraud or chargebacks happen. if fora becomes aware of a high risk booking fora will reach out to the advisor for details about the clients and bookings requesting additional documentation. advisors who have been the victim of fraud or something that seems suspicious (whether it’s the behavior of a client, partner or another advisor) should email support@fora.travel. fora advisor responsibility in client disputes if unable to resolve client fraud or chargeback issues with the client and the partner, the advisor will be held responsible for any resulting losses incurred by the partner and passed on to fora. if fora reaches out to an advisor for additional information related to fraud or chargebacks, a response is required within 72 hours. failure to respond in a timely manner could result in an advisor’s bookings being cancelled, particularly if there are fraud concerns. financial accountability if a chargeback dispute is not resolved in favor of the partner: the advisor is responsible for reimbursing the partner the full amount of the chargeback. fora reserves the right to pay the partner directly on the advisor’s behalf and recover the amount by offsetting future commissions due to the advisor. fora advisors are responsible for the bookings that they make and the clients that they manage. learn more about detecting and preventing fraud here.

title: Partner Engagement Policy

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: At Fora, we call suppliers partners for a reason. We work together to deliver exceptional experiences for your clients. When a Fora Advisor reaches out to a partner for a special client request or site visit, the community counts on the advisor to maintain high standards that strengthen our industry relationships.

sections.heading: Partner Contacts
paragraphs: Fora Advisors are equipped from their first day to book travel, VIP their clients, and engage with partners. Over time, advisors will naturally build relationships with the partners they work with most. These connections are valuable and should be maintained with care, professionalism, and thoughtful communication.
To support advisors at every stage, we have outlined clear guidelines by status that explain how to access partner information to best serve their clients.

sections.heading: Uncertified, Certified and Advanced Advisors
paragraphs: Uncertified, Certified and Advanced advisors should reach out to the property’s reservations team to VIP clients. Advisors should not include the Director of Sales or General Manager on VIP emails.
Advisors should use weekly instructor-led partner trainings, on-demand webinars in Portal, the partner website, and Google to find contact information for reservations teams.

sections.heading: Pro and X Advisors
paragraphs: Pro and X advisors have access to contact information for sales representatives and senior operational team members through their Virtuoso account and other partner directories.

Experienced advisors should only reach out to senior hotel team members when they have exhausted all other contacts. Advisors should not contact the Director of Sales to VIP clients. These contacts are best used to escalate service issues or problems on the rare occasion that it can not be solved by the front desk or reservations teams.

sections.heading: Partner Logins
paragraphs: As the business of a Fora Advisor grows, they will gain access to more in-depth preferred partner directories including Virtuoso, Four Seasons, Rosewood and Marriott. Preferred partner logins provide advisors with additional training resources and property level contacts.
Learn more about requesting partner logins here.

sections.heading: Uncertified, Certified and Advanced Advisors
paragraphs: Uncertified, Certified and Advanced advisors are eligible for some partner logins. Fora Advisors can request partner logins using the link above.

sections.heading: Pro and X Advisors
paragraphs: Pro and X advisors are eligible for preferred partner logins, including but not limited to:
Virtuoso: A Virtuoso account will be created by Fora's support team as part of the Pro onboarding. No action is required.

Four Seasons: When an advisor reaches Pro status and makes five unique bookings (clients and dates) with Four Seasons they may reach out to support@fora.travel to receive a Four Seasons Preferred Partner login.
Once an advisor adds their Four Seasons Advisor ID (FSID) to Portal, the FSID will be automatically added to any future Four Seasons bookings made in Portal.
Rosewood: When an advisor reaches Pro status, they will receive instructions on how to create a Rosewood Elite login.

sections.heading: X Advisors
paragraphs: X Advisors are eligible for additional preferred partner personal logins:

Marriott: Fora X advisors are eligible for a Marriott’s STARS and LUMINOUS login along with access to Marriott Guardian Angels contacts. Fora Advisors will receive instructions on how to register once they reach Fora X.

sections.heading: Notice of Confidentiality
paragraphs: Preferred partner rates and how to access them are confidential. Booking instructions or codes can not be shared publicly with anyone who is not a Fora Advisor.
Learn where to add your Four Season ID here.
Learn more about how to create your Rosewood login here.

sections.heading: Partner Events
paragraphs: Fora Advisors may be invited to partner-hosted events based on factors such as sales performance, location, and event context. These invitations are an opportunity to deepen relationships with partners and experience their offerings firsthand.

Partner-hosted events are organized and run directly by our supplier partners. These are distinct from Fora-hosted community events, which are organized by Fora and may include supplier participation.

Advisors must be directly invited by a partner or Fora HQ in order to attend a partner-hosted event. Unless otherwise stated on the invitation, invitations are non-transferable and intended only for the advisor named.

sections.heading: Uncertified, Certified, and Advanced Advisors
paragraphs: Uncertified, Certified and Advanced advisors are not eligible to attend partner events.

sections.heading: Pro and X Advisors
paragraphs: Pro and X advisors are eligible to attend partner events.
If you are invited by a partner prior to reaching Pro, please reach out to support@fora.travel.

sections.heading: Site Visits
paragraphs: Site visits allow Fora Advisors to tour hotel rooms and facilities during business hours. Cruise lines also offer site visits when ships are docked between sailings. This helps advisors discover unique features and learn about our partners enabling them to best match them with their clients' needs.

sections.heading: Uncertified Advisors
paragraphs: Uncertified advisors are not eligible to attend or organize  site visits.

sections.heading: Certified and Advanced Advisors
paragraphs: Certified and Advanced advisors are eligible to attend site visits and organize site visits for themselves.

sections.heading: Pro and X Advisors
paragraphs: Pro and Fora X advisors are eligible to attend site visits for themselves and organize site visits for other Fora Advisors.

sections.heading: Guidelines
paragraphs: Before reaching out to the partner, advisors organizing a site visit for other Fora advisors should email support@fora.travel and their local Chapter Leader (if applicable) with the property name, suggested date and proposed plan.
Advisors should be mindful of the following:

Schedule appropriately: Site visits should be planned at least 2 weeks in advance and hosted during normal business hours—Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM.  Sometimes a supplier will suggest a last minute site visit – which is okay, but if you are asking to schedule, please try to ask at least 2 weeks in advance.
Confirm in advance: Reconfirm the site visit 1–3 days before the scheduled time. If there are any changes, notify the partner contact as soon as possible.
Limit group size: If organizing a site visit for multiple advisors, the group should be limited to eight people or fewer, including the organizing advisor.
Follow up: Send a thank-you note to the hosting partner after the site visit.
Deliverables: Following a site visit, please leave a review for the partner in Portal.
Learn more about site visits here.
Learn more about reviews by advisors here.

title: Industry Benefits Policy

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Fora Advisors have access to industry benefits designed to deepen their expertise, strengthen partner relationships, and support their long-term success. As advisors grow their client base and establish their book of business, advisor benefits evolve in line with advisor status.

To ensure clear and consistent expectations within the Fora community, this policy outlines eligibility and guidelines for Travel Agent (TA) rates, net rates, and complimentary stays with hotel and cruise partners, along with Destination Management Companies (DMCs).
This policy also includes information on Familiarization (FAM) trips, travel conferences, CLIA membership, preferred partner programs, and special opportunities like Virtuoso Voyage Hosts.

sections.heading: Travel Agent Rates
paragraphs: Travel Advisor (TA) rates refer to discounted, net, or complimentary rates offered for self-bookings. These rates are a strategic sales tool designed to help advisors gain firsthand experience with partners, including hotels, cruise lines, and Destination Management Companies (DMCs). Advisors using TA rates are expected to have either previously booked clients with the partner or have plans to do so in the near future.

sections.heading: Uncertified, Certified and Advanced Advisors
paragraphs: Uncertified, Certified, and Advanced advisors are not eligible for TA rates.  Advisors must respectfully decline all related offers even if extended after completing a partner’s training (e.g. Disney).

sections.heading: Pro and X Advisors
paragraphs: Pro and X advisors are eligible for TA rates once they have already made a client booking with that partner or expect to do so in the coming months.

sections.heading: Uncertified Advisors
paragraphs: Uncertified Advisors are not eligible for TA Rates

sections.heading: Certified, Advanced, Pro and Fora X Advisors
paragraphs: Certified, Advanced, Pro and Fora X Advisors who have sold at least $10,000 in commissionable cruise revenue in the past year are eligible for TA rates.

sections.heading: Hotels
paragraphs: Pro or X advisors should email support@fora.travel before submitting a TA rate request and be mindful of the following guidelines:
Non-Peak Dates: Requests should only be made for non-peak dates. Advisors should refrain from asking for discounts during high seasons like spring break, summer, festive seasons or holiday weekends.
Room Type: Room requests should be for one standard or entry-level room only.
Short Stays: Stays are limited to one or two nights. Advisors should not request longer discounted stays or for more than one room (though having a guest in the room is generally allowed).

Client Demand: TA rates should only be requested from partners where the advisor has already sent clients and there is demonstrated interest from their client base. It's not appropriate to ask for agent rates at properties, partners or destinations that have never been booked by the advisor. This is a sales tool and the expectation is that the advisor will be able to sell the property thereafter.
Annual Limit: Each advisor may use up to 10 TA rates or complimentary stay room nights per year, not including FAM trips.
Deliverables: During the stay, advisors should plan to meet with hotel sales staff, tour the property, and review the property in Portal.
Bartering: Offering services of any kind (e.g. content creation) in exchange for discounted or free stays is prohibited.

sections.heading: Destination Management Companies (DMCs)
paragraphs: All Destination Management Companies (DMCs) in Portal belong to Fora's Preferred Partner program. Preferred partner DMCs provide gross rates that include a 12% commission for the advisor and accept payments directly from the advisor’s clients. When booking a DMC for personal travel, Fora Advisors are eligible for different levels of access based on advisor status.
Learn more about DMCs through the training here and help center article here.
Net Rates with a DMC for Personal Travel may be requested after completing at least one booking with that specific DMC.
Personal travel is defined as a booking made for the advisor and their immediate family or friends.

sections.heading: Cruise
paragraphs: Certified, Advanced, Pro and X Advisors who have sold at least $10,000 in commissionable cruise bookings in the last year should follow the below guidelines when requesting and accepting TA rates.
Some cruise lines offer a set discount that can be used on many itineraries. In most cases it will be a flat rate with only specific sailings and cabin types available.
To find cruise-specific TA rates and requirements, check the cruise line’s advisor portal, where rates and policies are often listed.
Please do not reach out to the cruise line Business Development Managers (BDMs) about TA rates. Advisors in need of assistance or BDM contact, should email support@fora.travel.

sections.heading: Cruise Line International Association Membership
paragraphs: The Cruise Lines International Association (CLIA) is the world’s largest cruise industry trade association. It represents cruise lines, travel advisors, port authorities, and cruise industry partners, working to advance the cruise sector worldwide.
Fora Advisors are able to book and earn commission on cruises without a CLIA membership by using Fora's IATA when booking through the cruise line's agent portal or phone line.

sections.heading: Uncertified Advisors
paragraphs: Uncertified Advisors are not eligible for a CLIA membership

sections.heading: Certified, Advanced, Pro and Fora X Advisors
paragraphs: Certified, Advanced, Pro and Fora X Advisors who have sold at least $10,000 in commissionable cruise revenue in the past year are eligible for a CLIA Membership.
Learn more about the benefits of and how to join CLIA here.

sections.heading: Familiarization (FAM) Trips
paragraphs: Familiarization trips (FAMs) are opportunities for advisors to gain firsthand knowledge of destinations and properties, build experiences to better serve their clients and expand their business. These events also foster industry connections and build a sense of community within Fora.
Since participation in these trips requires a substantial time commitment, advisors should carefully consider their availability before applying and confirming attendance.

sections.heading: Uncertified, Certified and Advanced Advisors
paragraphs: Uncertified, Certified, and Advanced advisors are not eligible to participate in FAM trips.

sections.heading: Pro and X Advisors
paragraphs: Pro and X advisors are eligible to participate in FAM trips.

sections.heading: Uncertified Advisors
paragraphs: Uncertified Advisors are not eligible for TA Rates

sections.heading: Certified, Advanced, Pro and Fora X Advisors
paragraphs: Certified, Advanced, Pro and Fora X Advisors who have sold at least $10,000 in commissionable cruise revenue in the past year are eligible to participate in FAM trips.

sections.heading: Partner FAMs
paragraphs: Partner FAMs are led and organized by a partner such as a DMC, Rep. Company, Hotel, Hotel Group, Cruise Line or other industry group. Here are a few key things to keep in mind:
Invitations and applications are organized through Fora, but often have specific acceptance requirements from the partner.
FAM priorities will be based on the partner who arranged the FAM, whether that be a hotel, cruise line or DMC.
Most of the time, an advisor will be the only Fora Advisor on the trip.
Advisors might have a limited destination experience based on the goals of the partner.
If a Fora Advisor is directly invited to a partner hosted FAM trip, they should email  support@fora.travel to notify Fora headquarters. Approval is not required for Pro/ X advisors.

sections.heading: Fora FAMs and Retreats
paragraphs: Fora FAMs are led and organized by Fora with a partner. Pro or X advisors can attend no more than two Fora FAMs and one Retreat per year. Advisors apply and are chosen to attend based on the following:

Production in the destination, a comparable destination or with a relevant partner (e.g. If Fora is hosting an IHG-led trip to Paris, selected advisors may have a strong booking history in Paris, with IHG properties, or in similar cities such as London or Rome)
Previous participation in Fora FAMs or Retreats, as well as demonstrated community engagement
Strength of the advisor’s application and rationale for attending
Volume of applications received and overall demand for the FAM or Retreat
Learn more about FAMs & Retreats here.

sections.heading: Conferences
paragraphs: Travel industry conferences help advisors deepen partner relationships in the industry. Conferences can be a meaningful milestone in an advisor’s journey, and Fora is here to provide support every step of the way.

sections.heading: Uncertified, Certified, and Advanced Advisors
paragraphs: Uncertified, Certified and Advanced advisors are not eligible to participate in travel industry conferences. Advisors must respectfully decline all offers.

sections.heading: Pro, and X Advisors
paragraphs: Pro and X advisors are eligible to participate in travel industry conferences.
*CLIA members are eligible to attend Cruise Conferences (Ex.Cruise360 and Cruise World).

sections.heading: Pro Advisors
paragraphs: Pro advisors who are in good standing with the community are welcome to apply for Virtuoso Travel Week. Fora headquarters will communicate the process and timeline but please note the following:
Virtuoso has their own requirements for attendance, which change yearly
Advisors are solely responsible for related costs including flights, accommodation, meals and registration

sections.heading: X Advisors
paragraphs: X advisors can request one hosted conference per year as follows:

Advisors must submit their request through the process managed by Fora headquarters. This begins late the summer prior (ie: Summer 2025 for the 2026 conference year) on a rolling basis. Fora headquarters will do its best to match each advisor with the most relevant conference. Most conferences have minimum revenue requirements or other standards for acceptance that they might not surface publicly.
Advisors should always check with Fora headquarters before applying to any conference, even if they receive an application or recommendation to apply directly.
Hosted conferences typically cover some or all costs (fees, hotel, airfare). Advisors are responsible for any remaining expenses.
Learn more about Conferences here.

title: Communications & Branding Policy

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: A Fora Advisor’s travel brand plays a key role in how they connect with clients and partners. This policy outlines how Fora advisors should communicate using their Fora email address, build a personal brand, and represent their affiliation clearly across platforms.

It also covers the use of logos (related to Fora and preferred partners), content creation standards, and best practices for social media. Whether creating guides, sharing photos, or promoting your services, these guidelines support building a strong, trusted presence— while staying aligned with Fora’s brand and community values.

sections.heading: Fora Branding and Affiliation
paragraphs: All advisors must describe their relationship with Fora as an “independent travel advisor of Fora Travel”, “powered by Fora Travel” or “affiliate of Fora Travel” wherever travel services are publicly marketed. On social media or when there is a limited character count, the advisor should include their name or brand and affiliation as “Fora” or “@foratravel” (e.g. Ali powered by @foratravel).
Advisors based in Seller of Travel states and Ontario are subject to additional regulations.
Learn more about Seller of Travel here and Ontario regulations here.

sections.heading: Fora Brand Usage
paragraphs: Fora Advisors are encouraged to use Fora’s logo and branding on Fora-approved marketing templates and Fora’s shareable assets found in Portal. This is the ideal way to leverage the Fora logo.

However, Fora Advisors may use the Fora logo to make custom business cards, email signatures, website footers, as long as the logo is always accompanied by the affiliation language above and the logo is used without distortion (combination with other images, change of ratio or color, etc.).

Fora Advisors are not permitted to use the Fora logo (including co-branding) on any other materials including custom merchandise, large signage, etc. If you have any specific use questions, please email support@fora.travel.

sections.heading: Advertising
paragraphs: Fora Advisors may reference their affiliation with Fora in their own advertisements, but may not create advertising targeting at any keywords that contain “Fora.” Fora can require that an advisor discontinue ads containing Fora’s trademarks or intellectual property.

sections.heading: Fora Email Address
paragraphs: A Fora Advisor’s @fora.travel email address is firstname.lastname@fora.travel.

Email communications between Fora Advisors and Fora headquarters (including support@fora.travel) or between Fora Advisors and travel partners (whether or not preferred partners) must be done through the @fora.travel email address. Advisors may use a personal or branded email address for communications with clients.

sections.heading: Advisor Branding
paragraphs: Fora Advisors do not need to have a custom travel brand or logo. While some advisors operate under their own name, others choose to create a branded business. Fora Advisors who do have a travel brand can submit custom brand names and logos in Portal to be approved by Fora headquarters. This allows advisors to display their travel brand which will appear on client-facing links such as itineraries, booking confirmations from Portal, Vault forms, and review requests.

Fora Advisors must have the intellectual property rights for all custom materials used in their brand, including images, names, logos and slogans. By submitting branding, Fora Advisors are responsible for Fora's losses and expenses if another person alleges their proprietary rights were violated or misappropriated.
Advisors based in Seller of Travel states and Ontario are subject to additional regulations.
Learn more about Seller of Travel here and Ontario regulations here.

sections.heading: Uncertified Advisors
paragraphs: Uncertified advisors are not eligible to upload personal branding in Portal.

sections.heading: Certified, Advanced, Pro and X Advisors
paragraphs: Certified, Advanced, Pro and X advisors are eligible to upload personal branding in Portal.

sections.heading: Guidelines
paragraphs: Including the brand “Fora” or any variation thereof is prohibited
Free of offensive or inappropriate content (at the discretion of Fora HQ)
Use of borrowed or lightly edited logos, slogans, or symbols from other companies is prohibited
Use of unaltered stock imagery (e.g., images without significant manipulation such as cropping or color grading) is prohibited
If a brand name or URL slug is the advisor’s personal name, the associated logo must be a distinct design and may not consist solely of a personal photo
Brand names and logos that reference medical affiliations or include terms such as “official” or “government” are prohibited
Inclusion of website domains (e.g., .com, .org) or hyperlinks in logos or slugs is prohibited

sections.heading: Use of Fora
paragraphs: The “Fora” name should not be used by Fora Advisors in their own business entity or trade name, business page (e.g. LinkedIn, Yelp or Google) or social media, unless describing their affiliation with Fora. For example, social media handles such as “@janefora” or “@foraadvisorjane,” are not permitted. Acceptable examples include  “@janethewanderer” or other custom names.
Learn how to add your brand name and logo in Portal here.
Learn how LLCs and custom brands affect E&O eligibility here.
*Note: Ontario, Canada based advisors are subject to regulations that limit the use of custom brands.
Learn more about regulations specific to Ontario based travel advisors here.

sections.heading: Preferred Partner Program Affiliation
paragraphs: Fora’s relationships with our Preferred Partners come with guidelines around how Fora Advisors can showcase these affiliations and benefits. To maintain strong industry relationships and align with Fora’s partner agreements, advisors must follow approved language and usage rules when referencing these partners in public-facing materials.

sections.heading: Uncertified, Certified, Advanced Advisors
paragraphs: Uncertified, Certified, and Advanced advisors are not eligible to showcase their affiliation with Virtuoso Member and Four Seasons in any public facing materials. This includes the use of the Virtuoso and Four Seasons Preferred Partner corporate or member logos in email signature, signature panel or business cards.

sections.heading: Pro and X Advisors
paragraphs: Pro and X advisors are eligible to showcase their affiliation with Virtuoso and Four Seasons in public facing materials. This includes the use of the Virtuoso Member and Four Seasons Preferred Partner logos in their email signature, signature panel or business cards.
When showcasing affiliation with Virtuoso please use the recommended format (ie. “John Doe, an independent affiliate of Fora Travel—a Virtuoso Member.”)

sections.heading: Uncertified, Certified, Advanced and Pro Advisors
paragraphs: Uncertified, Certified, Advanced and Pro advisors are not eligible to feature the Marriott STARS & LUMINOUS logo in public facing materials including email signature, signature panel or business cards.

sections.heading: X Advisors
paragraphs: X advisors are eligible to feature Marriott STARS & LUMINOUS in public facing materials including email signature, signature panel or business cards.
Please see Fora headquarters approved signature templates here.

sections.heading: Advertisement of Partner Relations & Benefits
paragraphs: Partner Affiliation: Advisors must clearly state that their access to Preferred Partner benefits is through their affiliation with Fora. They may not imply that they, their businesses, or their websites—including the Client Portal—are official partners of any hotel, travel partner, or brand, and may reference benefits only using approved language:
“When you book Four Seasons through Fora, you will enjoy exclusive Four Seasons Preferred Partner benefits. Your advisor will be pleased to give you more details.”

Rates, Benefits & Promotions: Advisors may not guarantee or imply that booking through Fora offers a lower rate than booking directly, or publicly promote specific rates, discounts, benefits, or promotions unless the partner is publicly advertising the same offer and its terms permit public promotion. Offers may not be described as exclusive to Fora unless expressly authorized, and all communications must be current and accurate.

Marketing & Client Acquisition: Advisors may not purchase or bid on advertising that uses a hotel’s, travel partner’s, or brand’s name, rates, benefits, or promotions, or use them in SEO, metadata, or similar tactics intended to attract public traffic.

sections.heading: Advisor Content
paragraphs: Fora Advisors are encouraged to create content, such as trip reports and guides, to showcase destination experience, style, and perspective. When creating content, whether on Fora’s platforms or on social media, advisors should adhere to the below guidelines.

sections.heading: Originality and Distinctiveness
paragraphs: All trip reports and guide content must be original, created by the advisor, and not published elsewhere to maintain uniqueness.

Publishing duplicative or overly similar content on multiple platforms (e.g., personal websites or blogs and foratravel.com) can negatively impact both the content's value and client engagement. Linking to Fora content is permitted, but advisors should refrain from copying and pasting — or even rewording — subject matter from their Fora-branded content, as this may result in a penalty from Google or other search engines.

Magic Content: Magic content offers a way for advisors to engage  clients through personalized, branded content. Magic content includes articles and fortravel.com landing pages that can be customized to display an advisor’s contact information. Links to magic content can be shared broadly, but the written content should not appear (in part or in full) on other websites.

Forum: Advisors are encouraged to actively participate on Forum, share suggestions and resources to support the broader community. To ensure the space remains aligned with Fora’s values and policies, Fora reserves the right to review, edit, or remove posts at its discretion.
Learn more about Magic Content here.

sections.heading: Photo Ownership
paragraphs: Fora Advisors must have the rights to use all photos submitted for travel guides and profiles which could be because the photos are their own photos, they have the rights to the photo, the photo is an approved photo supplied by a hotel for marketing use, or the photo comes from free stock-photo resources, such as Unsplash or Pexels.

Hotel and Destination Images: Advisors should not use photos from hotel websites. Instead, advisors must use their own images, images supplied by hotels that are shown on the Advisor Portal, or free photos from Unsplash or Pexels.
All Other Content: Advisors should not use content created by other advisors or creators as their own.

sections.heading: Editorial Rights
paragraphs: Fora has a perpetual, non-exclusive right to use any content submitted by advisors. This content includes travel guides and profiles for publication on foratravel.com as well as reviews of suppliers for publication on the Advisor Portal. Fora may edit or remove content to meet brand guidelines and best practices including, but is not limited to, editing or removing content related to medical, religious and sex tourism, unauthorized photos of children, or unethical practices in tourism settings.

Post-Publication Review: Advisors should carefully review their content before submission. After publication, advisors should review their content to ensure everything is correct. If there are errors, advisors should email support@foratravel.com to request corrections.
Use After Subscription Ends: If an advisor leaves or is offboarded, Fora retains the right to use the content submitted by the advisor
Note: This does not refer to Fora-provided templates.

sections.heading: Social Media
paragraphs: Social Media can be a great tool to drive engagement with clients and prompt travel demand. Fora Advisors must tag or attribute the content when reposting material created by others.
Learn more about Fora’s approach to reposting advisor content here.

sections.heading: Media & Press Opportunities
paragraphs: We love celebrating our advisors and sharing your expertise with the world. To protect you, Fora and the broader community, we have a few simple guidelines for press.

As a general rule of thumb, Press is considered any opportunity where you are being identified and/or promoted as a Fora advisor or your connection to Fora is clear on someone else’s media channel. This can include but is not limited to Interviews or quotes for articles, blogs or newsletters, Podcasts, TV, radio or livestreams, Panels, talks or webinars that highlight you as a travel advisor

Fora Advisors should not accept or seek out any press opportunities without Fora’s knowledge or prior approval. We ask Advisors to please email support@fora.travel to review the request. We’ll confirm if it’s a fit, help with messaging if needed, and make sure everyone is protected.
Furthermore, Fora periodically receives press opportunities from our partners. As a certification benefit, Fora X advisors are eligible to receive first priority if inbound press opportunities.
Please refer to the help center for more information on press .

title: Conflict of Interest Policy

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Fora is committed to maintaining a transparent, trustworthy, and collaborative community. Advisors are expected to act in the best interest of their clients and the Fora community at all times. Activities that create, or appear to create, a conflict of interest with Fora’s mission, community, or operations are strictly prohibited.
To uphold these values, we have established how Fora Advisors share and promote services, both their own and those of closely related parties within the Fora network.

Fora Advisors are welcome to share objective insights, experiences, and expertise about travel partners. To ensure recommendations are made with transparency, we have outlined how to navigate other personal or business relationships while maintaining trust and professionalism within the Fora community.
Learn more about examples of promotion here.

sections.heading: Advisors Who Own or Work For a Travel-related Business
paragraphs: Advisors who own, operate, or are employed by another travel-related company or partner including but not limited to agencies, consortia, hotels, representative companies and tourism board entities must disclose this information upon onboarding or as soon as the affiliation begins by emailing support@fora.travel.

Fora has a strict zero-tolerance policy regarding promotion of an owned travel-related company inside the Fora community. Any advisor found to be promoting another business, product, or service within the Fora community without prior written approval will be subject to immediate review and potential offboarding. This includes, but is not limited to, posting links, offers, or solicitations in community channels or directly contacting advisors for business purposes.

sections.heading: Content Creators, Influencers and Bloggers
paragraphs: Fora supports creativity and recognizes that many advisors are content creators, writers or influencers who share travel experiences online. However, when content and promotion initiatives intersect with your role as a Fora Advisor, it must be handled carefully to avoid conflicts of interest, misrepresentation or ethical breaches.

In-person engagements and content connected to Fora’s partners should be handled in a professional manner, consistent with the Company’s brand values and reputation, and in a way that avoids any conduct that could reasonably be expected to harm the Company’s or a partner’s goodwill, brand or public image.

Offering or accepting free or discounted travel, accommodations, or other benefits in exchange for content creation (e.g., social posts, reviews, photography, videos) is considered bartering and is prohibited when connected to your Fora Advisor role. If you are compensated, hosted, or collaborating with a property, supplier, or brand in any capacity outside Fora, that relationship must remain distinct from your Fora advisor business.
Learn more about the types of content creation that is permitted here.

title: Policies & Community Guidelines

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: The Fora community of advisors is one of the things which makes Fora special. We expect every Fora Advisor to be a good steward of the community and be aware of and follow the community guidelines and policies outlined below.

The policies exist to create a framework that ensures our community can thrive together. If we learn of behavior that is not in accordance with guidelines and policies, we will reach out with a formal reminder. We reserve the right to take further action such as suspending membership or revoking membership entirely depending on the circumstances.

sections.heading: Community Guidelines
paragraphs: We are a community
We believe we can go further together.
We’re better together. We all give to the community as much as we get from the community– online and offline.
We operate with the highest level of integrity with clients, fellow Fora Advisors, travel partners, and others in the industry including advisors from other agencies.
We are building a culture of positivity and responsibility. Fora Advisors are expected to ask questions or raise issues in respectful ways, assuming best intentions of all participants.
We were all beginners once. Practice empathy and kindness. Be generous with your advice and ideas.
We call suppliers partners for a reason. They do not work for us. We work together to deliver exceptional experiences for our clients.
We work in partnership between Fora headquarters, advisor and travel partner communities to create a win-win-win outcome for all.
We are professionals
We engage with colleagues, travel partners, and each other respectfully and professionally.
For in-person events, we show up on time, prepared and dressed professionally. Fora headquarters and our partners note repeat no-show and late cancellations.
For online events, kindly enable your camera and ensure you are muted when not speaking.
A lot of consideration has been given to our approach to advisor status and benefits. We don't ask for or accept freebies or discounts outside of what’s stated in our Industry Benefits policy.
We are all travel entrepreneurs
Entrepreneurship is hard work and there are no shortcuts to building a travel business.
Fora headquarters and the community are here to help. However, we expect resourcefulness in everything we do. Search Forum, the Help Center, Sidekick (or Google) before asking a question.
Each one of us is a reflection of ourselves and Fora – from the tone of an email to how a complicated partner situation is managed. Be mindful of the impression you are making on others.
We are different on purpose
We are not trying to build a traditional travel agency.
We bring energy and enthusiasm to all interactions.
We are building our own, unique businesses. That diversity is a core strength and supports both partners and clients.
Fora’s community and sales growth enables our investments in systems and support.
